Les conséquences peuvent être graves et: The consequences can be serious and can go as far as a patient not being treated properly.
Les audiences pour l’enquête publique su: Over the past few days, the public inquiry hearings into the death of Joyce Echaquan have painted a picture of a reality that many people experience in the health care system. These are no longer isolated cases: many people face discrimination from health care staff because of their skin colour, gender, sexual orientation, weight, disability and more.
Les conséquences peuvent être graves et: The consequences can be serious and can go as far as a patient not being treated properly. When you're at risk of discrimination, how can you protect yourself while seeking treatment? We spoke with experts and with people who have lived through this kind of situation.
<strong>Avant de se rendre dans un établ: Before going to a health care facility
« On n’est pas toujours la personne la p: “We're not always the best person to stand up for ourselves, especially if we feel vulnerable, anxious, fragile or uncomfortable,” says Édith Bernier, an author, consultant and activist against fatphobia. She believes that being accompanied by someone you trust can reduce the risk of being discriminated against if you are likely to be. Having a loved one there means having a witness and an advocate in case of an incident. Unfortunately, COVID-19 health rules can make this more difficult.
Lorsque cela est possible, Mme Bernier s: When possible, Ms. Bernier also suggests making a list of questions to ask the treating staff. She says this helps steer the conversation and bring it back to the real subject of the discussion, that is, the reason for the appointment. “You can ask how the proposed solution is the only one, or the most effective one, for the problem you have,” she says.
Les patients peuvent-ils se prévaloir de: Can patients exercise their rights, which are too often poorly known, in a hospital setting? Did you know that you can refuse care? Asked about this, Quebec's Ministry of Health and Social Services said that, generally, a refusal form must be signed and placed in the patient's file.
Le patient doit également consentir à re: Patients must also consent to receiving care. “Even if you've given your consent for something, even if you've signed, you can withdraw it at any time,” explains Ariane Métellus, a consultant in perinatal care and in sexual, reproductive and perinatal health. She says consent must be obtained for every intervention when you are being treated in hospital.
« C’est le devoir des professionnels de: “It's the duty of health care professionals,” the consultant stresses. A patient can also ask for a second opinion, change medication or be transferred to another facility. According to the Ministry of Health, patients must discuss this with the care team on site, because protocols and procedures vary from one department to another.
« Chaque établissement a ses façons de f: “Each facility has its own way of doing things; patients can find out about them by speaking with the teams on site,” say the health authorities. Unfortunately, acting preventively does not rule out the possibility of an incident. “<l1>Mireille Ndjomouo</l1> is an example of someone who made her rights known. It's very telling,” laments Ariane Métellus. The mother, whose death is the subject of an inquiry, had not been allowed to have anyone with her for most of her hospital stay.
L’équipe médicale doit inscrire plusieur: The medical team must record several things in the patient's file. The rules on what information must be entered in a file vary depending on the facility and the professional's ethical obligations. “They have to write down what is done and what is administered, but also what the patient refuses, whether it's a treatment or an intervention,” explains Ms. Métellus. The consultant recommends making sure of this by saying, for example: “You're refusing me this, and I want it written in my file.”
Mme Métellus recommande également de pos: Ms. Métellus also recommends asking questions about the risks, the benefits and the alternatives, as well as about the risks tied to a proposed or imposed treatment, intervention or protocol.
« Ça fait partie du consentement », juge: “That's part of consent,” she says. The consultant also advises patients to take notes in a personal notebook to document everything they go through. For her part, Édith Bernier suggests recording conversations with medical staff when you feel threatened.
Le dossier médical d’un patient lui appa: A patient's medical file belongs to them and can be consulted at any time. “It's important to do so to get an idea of the facts and obtain other information,” sums up Ms. Métellus. The<l1> Carnet santé</l1> gives access to some information online. If the medical file is held at a hospital or a CLSC, you can get access by making a request to the facility's records department.
En général, les dossiers de patients dét: In general, patient files held by a hospital must be kept for a minimum of five years after the last entry in the file.
« La discrimination, c’est contraire à l: “Discrimination is contrary to the Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms,” says Geoffroy Guilbaut, a lawyer specializing in liability. In the event of a discriminatory incident, he suggests filing a complaint with the Quebec Human Rights and Youth Rights Commission, which will investigate. The process is free and can be started by an individual or by an organization on behalf of a complainant.
Si la Charte protège les individus contr: While the Charter protects individuals against discrimination based on ethnicity, age, sexual orientation or religion, for example, weight and appearance are not listed, says Édith Bernier, who is campaigning to have them added. Patients who feel they received inadequate or discriminatory service at a health and social services facility can also contact the facility's <l1>complaints and service quality commissioner</l1>. “The complaints that are taken into consideration aim to change practices. No action will be taken against the health care professional named in the complaint,” notes Ariane Métellus, a consultant in reproductive and sexual health. To file a complaint, you can get help from complaint assistance and support centres (CAAP). The consultant also offers a complaint support service.
« Il y a toute cette éducation à faire a: “There is a whole education effort to be made around the complaint process,” says Ms. Métellus, who considers the process to be difficult and long. “These are not easy steps to take. The system is poorly adapted, just like for people who file complaints about sexual violence. It's the same for people who have experienced violence in the health care system,” she believes. If a caregiver says or does things that cause harm, you can also turn to the caregiver's professional order, such as the Collège des médecins or the Ordre des infirmières et infirmiers du Québec. Doctors and nurses are governed by their codes of ethics, and it is possible to file a complaint against an individual who breaches them.
Par exemple, le code de déontologie des: For example, the physicians' code of ethics states that they must fulfill their professional obligations with integrity and with respect for dignity. On the legal side, a patient can bring a civil liability action if they believe a health care professional committed a fault that caused them harm. Because a lawsuit can be costly and complex, Guilbault recommends that patients file a complaint.
« L’accès aux réseaux, qui n’est pas du: “Turning to social networks, which isn't a legal avenue, is often effective,” says Geoffroy Guilbault. He points out that speaking out online can shed light on a situation and also show a community's concern, as we have seen. Giving people a voice is what Tori Ford, founder of Medical Herstory, wants to do. The platform invites participants to share their diverse perspectives and experiences in a trauma-informed environment. To fight the problem, Ms. Ford favours self-advocacy, helping patients navigate the medical world.
C’est sa propre expérience dans le systè: It was her own experience in the health care system, following chronic health problems, that prompted her to launch the platform in 2018. “I started hearing about so many other people who had faced sexism, racism and ableism in the medical world,” says the founder. At the time, there was nowhere to share such stories. Corinne Jacquet, a lawyer at the Saint-Michel legal clinic, believes this subject needs to be talked about more. “Often, people experience medical racism and don't know that's what they're going through. They have traumatic or disturbing experiences, but they move on, even though they've just experienced a form of stigmatization and systemic racism,” she tells us. When the irreparable happens, the case goes to the coroner.
« Le mandat du coroner n’est pas de dist: “The coroner's mandate is not to assign blame, but to prevent other similar situations,” stresses Geoffroy Guilbault. That is how the 2019 death of Akeem Scott was described as preventable in coroner Karine Spénard's report, released recently.
